title: finding(core): `chartConfigPresentation` DROPS an inline-locale-map `title`/`subtitle`/`description`, so a dashboard/report chart authored in the spec's own `I18nLabel` union renders with no heading at all
body:
Found while fixing objectui#8943 (the sibling defect in `normalizeChartSchema`'s `label()`). Filed rather than fixed there: different package, different function, and a different failure mode — 8943 renders the WRONG language, this one renders NOTHING.

## The defect

`packages/core/src/utils/chart-presentation.ts` lowers an authored chart config's chrome onto the chart schema the dataset-bound surfaces hand the renderer. Its `title` / `subtitle` / `description` limbs go through a local `text()` helper that accepts **only a plain string**:

```ts
const text = (v: unknown): string | undefined => (typeof v === 'string' && v ? v : undefined);

if (typeof config.showLegend === 'boolean') out.showLegend = config.showLegend;
const title = text(config.title);
if (title) out.title = title;
const subtitle = text(config.subtitle);
if (subtitle) out.subtitle = subtitle;
const description = text(config.description);
if (description) out.description = description;
```

The function's own docblock says it lowers the keys of "spec `ChartConfigSchema` / `ReportChartSchema` — the same keys on both". `@objectstack/spec` types `ChartConfigSchema.title` as `I18nLabel` — a plain string **OR** an inline locale map — so this is authored surface, not an accident:

```json
{ "chartConfig": { "title": { "zh-CN": "定价", "en": "Pricing" } } }
```

`text()` returns `undefined` for the map arm, the `if (title)` guard skips the assignment, and the key never reaches `out`. The chart then draws with **no heading**, in every language, with no diagnostic. The author wrote spec-legal metadata and the runtime discarded it silently.

Note the shape of it: this is not the wrong-language bug. `title` is not resolved badly, it is **not resolved at all** — so it is invisible to any check that asks "does the heading match the locale", because there is no heading to compare.

## Reachability — measured, not assumed

`chartConfigPresentation` has two live call sites, both on paths a user reaches:

- `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DatasetWidget.tsx` — `chartConfigPresentation(widget?.chartConfig, categoryColors)`, i.e. a dashboard widget's own `chartConfig`.
- `packages/plugin-report/src/DatasetReportRenderer.tsx` — `chartConfigPresentation(chart, categoryColors)` (which then destructures `title` away, so the report surface is affected for `subtitle` / `description` only).

Neither resolves these three keys through `pickLocalized` first. Both files DO import `pickLocalized` and use it — `DatasetWidget` for `options.description`, `DatasetReportRenderer` for measure labels — so the resolver is already in scope at both call sites; these three keys simply do not route through it.

## Why this is not covered by the neighbouring ledger

`chart-presentation.ts` also holds `labelText()`, a deliberate first-string-wins pick for series labels and axis titles. That one IS documented and ledgered — the file states that this package is React-free, holds no i18n provider, and that "a caller that CAN resolve the language resolves the label itself and overrides the merged one; see objectui#4020". That mitigation is a real design and this card does not reopen it.

`text()` is a different thing and is not covered by it: it does not make a locale-unaware PICK that a caller can override — it **erases the value**, so there is nothing left for any caller to re-resolve. The override route the `labelText` ledger relies on is unavailable by construction.

## Suggested shape (not a ruling)

The React-free constraint that shapes `labelText` applies here too, so "call `pickLocalized` in `@object-ui/core`" is not obviously the answer. Two directions, both needing a decision rather than a guess:

1. Carry the value through unresolved (widen the lowered key to the `I18nLabel` union) and resolve at the two render sites, both of which already hold a language. This matches the route objectui#8943 rejected for its own site and the route `labelText`'s ledger assumes.
2. Give `chartConfigPresentation` an optional `language` parameter and resolve through `pickLocalized`, the way `normalizeChartSchema` now does (objectui#8943, PR objectui#9039). Both existing callers are components and can supply one.

Whichever is taken, the acceptance is that a spec-legal locale-map `title` reaches the DOM as a heading in the viewer's language, and that `pickLocalized` stays the single resolver for the union.

## Acceptance

- A dashboard widget whose `chartConfig.title` is an inline locale map renders a heading, in the active language, for at least two languages.
- The same for `subtitle` and `description` on both the dashboard and report surfaces.
- A plain-string `title` is unchanged.
- Whatever is left unresolved on purpose is ledgered by name with a reason, as `labelText`'s neighbouring case already is.

Refs: objectui#8943, objectui#4020.

Reported from the os-dev seat while landing PR objectui#9039; session reference `session_01MPaVWWMuWeT5LgB1qoXjVB`. Generated with Claude Code.
